newsitem.title: CHINA: China nuclear plant passes IAEA safety appraisal.
newsitem.headline: China nuclear plant passes IAEA safety appraisal.

text.p: China's Daya Bay nuclear power plant bordering Hong Kong has passed a nuclear safety appraisal by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) after closure earlier this year, the Xinhua news agency said.
"IAEA...made a three-week examination, and concluded that the power station is operating strictly in accordance with international safety standards," Xinhua said late on Friday.
IAEA would submit to the Chinese government a detailed technical report on the appraisal in three months, Xinhua quoted K. Hide, head of the inspection team, as saying.
The IAEA inspection team consisted of 16 nuclear experts from the United States, Britain, Hungary and the Netherlands, Xinhua said.
The plant was shut down for the second time in a year in March when problems with the Unit Two exciter coincided with refuelling of Unit One.
Officials have said problems with the exciter were not related to safety or radioactivity. The plant resumed operation in April.
The plant went into commercial operation in 1994 to the anger of anti-nuclear protesters in Hong Kong.

By October 24, the plant had provided 9.3 million megawatt-hours to power grids, with the amount in the whole of 1996 expected to be 10-15 million megawatt-hours, Xinhua said. It gave no further details.
